wars.name: Isanavarman's wars against the Huns, Gaudas, Andhras and Sulikas
wars.outcome: Isanavarman 'defeated them in battle' (the Alchon Huns); the Haraha inscription of 554 records 'further military victories against the Gaudas, Andhras and Sulikas'. No land is named and no date for the Hun defeat.

wars.name: Maukhari-Later Gupta rivalry over Magadha
wars.outcome: The Maukharis 'had a rivalry with the Later Guptas of Magadha'; the Aphsad inscription credits a Later Gupta king with defeating Maukhari elephant forces. The page dates none of it; the later-gupta-dynasty dossier has Sharvavarman invade Magadha c. 575.
wars.note: Years are the reigns of Sharvavarman and Grahavarman, not dates of fighting.

wars.name: Fall of Kannauj
wars.outcome: Grahavarman was killed by Devagupta of Malwa c. 605; Bakker's 'confederation of all those who held a grudge' attacked Kanyakubja (Shashanka page); Rajyavardhana was killed c. 606; Harsha, ruler of Thanesar from 606, then attacked Kannauj.

certainty.note: No frontier is described beyond 'Thaneshwar in the West to Nalanda district in the east'; Cliopatria's outline follows the Gupta heartland.

notes: Two pages. Cliopatria's 555-611 shape is the entire last Gupta shape (2,051 cells) and reaches Bengal, Odisha and Chhattisgarh; the page limits the kingdom to Thaneshwar-Nalanda, so those lands are cut (West Bengal and Bangladesh go to gauda-kingdom, Odisha and Chhattisgarh to nobody). Jharkhand (295 cells) and Nepal (116) were left as drawn: the page is silent. Cliopatria's Gupta shape (554) is the predecessor. The page is thin on dates: no reign years for Harivarman, Adityavarman, Isvaravarman or Avantivarman, and two dates for Sharvavarman's accession (c. 560 in the text, c. 574 in the list), so no rulers list is given. The end is c. 606 (infobox); Cliopatria's 607-611 shape is left to harsha-s-empire (sa-03), which should start at 606 (Thanesar) and take Kannauj. The later-gupta-dynasty dossier has Sharvavarman take Magadha c. 575 and Harsha restore it c. 606; this page does not date that and Cliopatria's shape holds Bihar from 555, so Magadha 555-574 is drawn Maukhari though the Later Guptas held it (unverified: page budget). 'Gaya' and Nalanda are places; Thanesar is a coordinate radius. 'pushyabhuti-dynasty' (Thanesar before 612) is named by the gupta-empire dossier and needs a dossier.
